ranking.name: Water running off the surface
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water running off the surface in East Africa changed by +0.0056 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval +0.0004 to +0.0109), which is statistically significant (p = 0.03). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.0139 mm/day.

ranking.name: Water leaving the land (evapotranspiration)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water leaving the land (evapotranspiration) in East Africa changed by +0.055 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval +0.001 to +0.112), which is statistically significant (p = 0.05). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.134 mm/day.

ranking.name: Rain and snow (precipitation)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, rain and snow (precipitation) in East Africa shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.46): the estimate is +0.05 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.07 to +0.17). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.
